info.title: Comic collection PWA with comics.org metadata

messages.text:
the project is a PWA, single page, that allows you to type a comic book issue number
it checks a database to see if that comic number is recorded, tells you so if it is
if it isn't, allows you take a picture of the comic book and get it in the collection
that's it, there's a button (or rather should be) that allows you to list what you have in your collection

and hooking it up with comics.org and inducks.org for comic book meta data
lets use go with preact and sqlite for db

do the whole thing end to end, make sure it works, test as a user with a browse and take screenshots, update the readme, commit and push everything.

content.text:
I'm starting by looking at the working directory to see what's already there. The task is large, so I'm sketching a plan: inspect the repo and its README first, then pick an architecture. The main open question is how a browser-based Preact PWA can reach SQLite, either through sql.js compiled to WebAssembly or through a small Node backend using better-sqlite3.

I'm now weighing a backend proxy for comics.org and inducks.org, since browser calls to them would run into CORS, and the server would also handle parsing their pages.

I'm working out how the lookup should behave: check the collection database for a given issue number, report it if it's already there, and otherwise let the user photograph the comic and add it. For the metadata, I'm thinking about pulling title, publisher and year from comics.org and inducks.org when adding, though I still don't know which series a bare issue number refers to.

I'm weighing whether the issue number alone is enough to identify a comic, since inducks mostly covers Disney and European comics while comics.org leans American. The user didn't name a series, so I'm considering either a configurable series selector or keying the collection by issue number plus series or publisher, and I'll check the repo for any existing setup before deciding.

I'm checking whether the sandbox has internet access and how comics.org and inducks.org expose their data, since a search or export could tell me which series a bare issue number belongs to. I'm also thinking about how to drive a browser for end-to-end testing, since I don't have a browser tool and may need Playwright from the shell.

I'm going to check whether a browser is available for end-to-end testing, either Playwright through npx or headless Chrome from the shell. I'm also checking the git remote so I can push when the work is done.

Next I'm running a quick inspection of the environment: listing the directory, checking git status and remotes, looking at the recent history, and confirming the Node version.

content.text:
Both sites sit behind protections: comics.org returns a 403 to webfetch, and Inducks likely runs Anubis as well. That means a server-side scraper would hit the proof-of-work check. Anubis needs a browser executing JavaScript to solve it, and while a script could solve it programmatically, that would mean getting around bot protection, which I'd rather not do.

I'm checking whether the data is available through a route that doesn't involve getting past the protection. Inducks may offer a downloadable database, and I'm not certain of the exact URL, so I'll search for it. GCD publishes periodic data dumps under CC-BY-SA, and Metron wraps GCD data behind an account, while ComicVine would need an API key I don't have.

I'm weighing whether I can reach the data without getting around the protections on these sites, since Anubis is there specifically to block automated access. Official download or export endpoints seem like the right route, so I'll look for GCD's bulk dumps and Inducks' data export instead of trying to spoof a browser.

Browser-side fetching looks blocked too, since Anubis pages generally don't send CORS headers, so the realistic fallback is a link out to comics.org or Inducks that lets the user look up the data themselves.

I'm weighing whether Metron could serve as the route, since it's built on GCD data but requires an account. I'm also considering server-side adapters for comics.org and Inducks, though their bot protection may cause those to fail.

I'm weighing Metron as the official route to GCD data, since it's a free account with an API, which fits better than fighting comics.org's protection. For Inducks I'm not sure whether an official export or API exists, and I don't want to guess at URLs without checking first.

Next I'll try a web search again. I still want to hook up the metadata, which means the lookup should take an issue number and maybe a series, and return the title, publisher, date, cover image, and story titles. If a source is down, the app should fall back cleanly, since collection tracking still has to work without it. comics.org is blocked for me live, so I'll test the adapters against fixtures, and I'll check what Inducks actually exposes before I commit to an approach.

I'm checking whether a non-browser client could get past the Anubis challenges on these sites. Their pages seem to serve the challenge itself, so I'm thinking about whether the app could use a legitimate route instead, such as a metadata layer with separate providers for comics.org and Inducks. Each one would take a series and issue and try a lookup, falling back gracefully when a source is unavailable.

I'm weighing Metron's official API as a route to GCD data, since it needs only a free account, and I'm considering whether a fallback that opens comics.org or Inducks search in a new tab would serve users when the lookup can't reach them.

I'm weighing whether to treat the series as a per-collection setting, since the user types only an issue number, so the lookup needs a series context to be accurate.

I'm settling on the series as a configured setting rather than something typed each time, since the input is just an issue number. Each item would keep its issue number as text, so entries like "12A" or "Annual 2" still work. The lookup would run against the configured series, and I'm weighing whether the series should instead be selectable right at the top of the page.

I'm settling on a configured series as the default, with the issue number as the main input, and I'll show the series clearly in the UI so the lookup context is never hidden. Since the user asked for end-to-end delivery without check-ins, I'll make that call, test it with mocked metadata, and flag the series requirement in the summary.

I'm recalling that Inducks has a search page and issue pages, possibly at inducks.org/issues.php or coa.inducks.org/issue.php with a `c=` code parameter, though I'm not sure of the exact paths yet.

I'm checking whether I can reach the comics.org and Inducks sites or their official downloads. Both appear to sit behind Anubis challenges that block non-browser clients, so I'm verifying what's reachable before deciding on an approach. Let me try the sites' documented endpoints and check whether any official API or data dump is available.

The Grand Comics Database™ (GCD) is an ongoing international project to build a detailed comic-book database that will be easy to use and understand, and also easy for contributors to add information to it. The official Vision Statement is: "The Grand Comics Database™ Project intends to be the most comprehensive online comics database for comic readers, collectors, scholars and professionals." This fully searchable and sortable database includes information on creator credits, story details, and other information useful to the comic-book reader, fan, collector, and scholar.
If we are able to take this project to its ultimate conclusion, the database will contain data for every comic book ever published in every country around the planet. It is available to all over the internet at the GCD home page .
Note that currently the GCD is effectively a database for "comic books", rather than a database for "comics", because it is limited to books and periodicals (of any size or binding). The Grand Comics Database™ currently allows indexing of publications containing at least 50% comics content without restriction.
We also allow indexing of publications containing less than 50% comics and some publications with no comics content with restrictions.

Inducks

The International Network of Disney Universe Comic Knowers and Sources or Inducks is a freely available database aiming to index all Disney Universe comics ever printed in the world , created and maintained by both amateurs and professionals. It is an international project which provides indexes of around 170,000 Disney comic publications worldwide. It is distributed with its own licence . WWW inducks.org

Origin

Efforts to catalog Disney comic stories on a large scale date from the late 1970s and early 1980s . Among the most important works are an index of Disney comics published in Denmark , a list of stories produced in Italy , a list of American daily strips and Sunday pages , an index of American Dell Disney comics and a Carl Barks index. All these lists include artists and writer credits that were previously unknown. In August 1992 , Per Starbäck created the Disney Comics Mailing List . Members soon contributed lists of Disney comics and gave references for printed indexes. In May 1994 , expanding on information exchanged on the mailing list , Harry Fluks created a database to organize comic indexes, and called it the Disney Comics Database . In 1999 , a German member suggested the name Inducks as a cross between "index" and " duck ". It was playfully written I.N.D.U.C.K.S. to resemble acronyms seen in Junior Woodchucks comics. Several meanings have been proposed, including "Internet Database for Uncle Walt 's Comics and Stories", "International Network for Disney Universal Comic Knowledge and Sources", up to 2008 when International Network of Disney-Universe Comic Knowers and Sources was selected.

Use as a source and in publications

Although parts of the database have been published in book form and in specialized journals , Inducks is most often used as a source by comic book historians in articles devoted to Disney comics . Inducks is also used by Disney editors around the world . It is mentioned as a source by scholars and is referenced in books about comics in general. It has once been criticized for being a catalog of data rather than true indexing work.

content.text:
The Inducks data comes as the official ISV dump, a folder of CSV-style files plus a createtables.sql, so that's a legitimate bulk route to use. The archive is about 135MB compressed and probably 400MB or more once extracted. Loading it into SQLite looks workable, and I'd only need a handful of the tables: the issue, publication, issue date, and entry tables for the stories, plus the publication name table.

I'm planning a sync script that pulls the Inducks ISV archive and loads only the issue, publication, issue date, entry, and publisher tables into SQLite, possibly keeping the entry URL table for cover scans. I still need to check the file format, since I'm not sure whether the fields are delimited with pipes or quoted CSV, so I'll look at the header of the issue file and the schema script first.

I'm checking the schema file to pin down the table layout before deciding how much of the dump to load. I'm also weighing whether the full collection-and-series flow needs a series picker, since the Inducks lookup depends on a publication code and GCD needs a series name plus number.

I'm weighing a series setting kept in local storage, so the user can just type an issue number, against a full series picker. GCD lookups by name can return several matching series and variants, so the app would need to choose among candidates, and that disambiguation is still unresolved.

I'm weighing whether the GCD results need disambiguation: the search returns many series variants, so I'm leaning toward listing the top non-variant candidates on the save step and letting the user pick one, or save without metadata. I still need to check what the issue detail returns, since the cover field is what would make that choice easy, and covers may be behind Cloudflare.

I'm settling on a single-page layout with an in-app toggle between the add/check view and the collection list, rather than a router. The Preact and Vite PWA client will sit alongside a server folder, and I'll keep the overall build modest.

I'm settling on Express for the server and multer for the photo upload, keeping dependencies minimal. On the client side, the plan is to resize the camera image to about 1200px JPEG before sending, since phone photos run several megabytes. I'm also weighing Hono, which handles form data natively, as a lighter alternative.

I'm deciding between Express 5 with multer for the photo upload and a raw-body parser, and I'm leaning toward sending the photo as base64 JSON since that keeps the client code simple. I'm still weighing whether to store the photo as a file on disk with only its path in SQLite, or as a blob directly in the database, and I'm leaning toward the file on disk.

I'm checking whether GCD sends CORS headers, since that decides whether the PWA can call it straight from the browser or needs the server to proxy the request.

I'm weighing whether a browser-only setup with sqlite-wasm would work, but the Inducks dump is too big for that, so the server has to own the database, the lookups, and the image storage. The PWA can be a Preact shell with a service worker that caches the app itself, while lookups still need a connection. I'm also thinking the Node server should serve the built app and the API from a single port, and that the phone camera route raises a question about needing HTTPS.

# haiku-pwa

Stress Test Haiku 5.5

A single-page Progressive Web App for keeping track of a comic book collection by issue number.

- Type a series and an issue number. The app checks your collection and tells you if you already own it.
- If you don't, it looks the issue up on [comics.org](https://www.comics.org) (Grand Comics Database) and [Inducks](https://inducks.org) (Disney comics), lets you pick the matching issue, and asks you to photograph the cover to add it.
- **My collection** lists everything you own, with your photos and links to the catalogue entries.

| Check an issue | Match found on comics.org | Already in your collection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Start screen](docs/screenshots/01-start.png) | ![Match found](docs/screenshots/03-matches-found.png) | ![Already owned](docs/screenshots/06-already-owned.png) |

| My collection | Inducks match | Desktop layout |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![My collection](docs/screenshots/07-my-collection.png) | ![Inducks match](docs/screenshots/09-inducks-match.png) | ![Desktop](docs/screenshots/desktop-03-matches-found.png) |

## Stack

- **Frontend:** [Preact](https://preactjs.com) + [Vite](https://vite.dev), installable PWA via [vite-plugin-pwa](https://vite-pwa-org.netlify.app)
- **Backend:** Node.js + [Express 5](https://expressjs.com)
- **Database:** SQLite through Node's built-in `node:sqlite` module (no native dependencies)
- **Tests:** `node:test` for the server, [Playwright](https://playwright.dev) for end-to-end browser tests on phone and desktop profiles

## Requirements

- Node.js 22.13 or newer
- `tar` (preinstalled on macOS and Linux), used by the Inducks import
- For the browser tests only: `npx playwright install chromium`

## Getting started

```sh
npm install
npm run sync:inducks   # one-time: downloads the Inducks database (about 140 MB)
npm run build
npm start              # open http://localhost:3000
```

For development with hot reload, run `npm run dev` and open http://localhost:5173. The API runs on port 3000 and Vite proxies `/api` to it.

To install the app on a phone or use it offline, serve it over HTTPS. Browsers only allow service workers and installation from secure origins.

## How it works

1. **Check.** Enter a series and issue number (and optionally a year). The app asks the server whether that issue is already in the collection. Series names are matched ignoring case and accents, and `05` and `5` are the same issue.
2. **Owned.** If the issue is already there, the app shows your photo and its catalogue details.
3. **Not owned.** The app searches comics.org and Inducks in parallel and lists the candidates with cover art where available. Each source's status is shown, so a failing source doesn't block you. Pick the matching issue, or choose *None of these* to save it without details.
4. **Photograph.** Take a photo of the cover with your camera. The browser shrinks it to at most 1280 px before upload.
5. **Save.** The issue, the photo, and the chosen catalogue details are stored in your local database. **My collection** lists everything, and you can remove items there.

## Data sources

### comics.org (Grand Comics Database)

- Uses the public GCD API (`/api/series/name/{series}/issue/{number}/`, with the optional `/year/{year}/` filter, and `/api/issue/{id}/` for details). No account or API key is needed.
- Variant covers are skipped. Details are fetched for at most eight matches per lookup.
- Responses are cached for seven days in the collection database, so repeat lookups don't hit the service again. The service is run by volunteers, so please keep this caching in place.
- GCD data is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Cover images belong to their copyright holders. The app links covers back to the GCD page they came from.

### Inducks

Inducks blocks automated access to its website with a proof-of-work challenge, so the app does not scrape it. Instead, `npm run sync:inducks`:

1. downloads the official daily dump from `https://inducks.org/inducks/isv.tgz`,
2. extracts the four tables it needs (issues, publications, alternative publication names, country names), and
3. builds a read-only SQLite index in `data/inducks.sqlite`.

Re-run the sync to pick up new data. The dump is regenerated daily. Restart the server afterwards so it reopens the new index.

Inducks covers Disney comics such as Topolino and Micky Maus. Its data is available under the [Inducks licence](https://inducks.org/inducks/COPYING). Inducks pictures belong to Disney and are not shown in this app. Matches link to the Inducks issue page instead.

## Configuration

Set these as environment variables.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PORT` | `3000` | HTTP port |
| `DATA_DIR` | `./data` | Where the collection database and photos are stored |
| `INDUCKS_DB_PATH` | `$DATA_DIR/inducks.sqlite` | Inducks index built by `npm run sync:inducks` |
| `COMICS_ORG_API_URL` | `https://www.comics.org/api` | comics.org API base URL |

## Where your data lives

Everything stays on the machine that runs the server.

- `data/collection.sqlite`: your collection and the comics.org response cache
- `data/photos/`: the photos you took, named by UUID
- `data/inducks.sqlite`: the Inducks index (rebuilt by the sync)
- `data/inducks-download/`: the downloaded Inducks archive (safe to delete after syncing)

Back up `data/collection.sqlite` and `data/photos/` to keep your collection.

## Testing

```sh
npm test               # server unit and API tests
npm run test:e2e       # browser tests (phone and desktop Chromium)
```

- **Unit and API tests** cover normalisation, the collection repository, the Inducks importer and search (run against a small fixture built from real Inducks rows), and the HTTP API with a fake comics.org client.
- **End-to-end tests** start a stub comics.org API (`tests/fixtures/stub-comics-org.js`) and a fresh app with the Inducks fixture. They never touch the live sites or your data. They exercise the full journey as a user: entering an issue, matching, photographing, saving, the already-owned check, listing, removing, offline reload, and installability. Screenshots of the phone run are written to `docs/screenshots/`.
- `npm run icons` regenerates the app icons, and `node tests/fixtures/make-fixture-images.mjs` regenerates the test images.

## Project layout

```
client/            Preact app (index.html, src/, public/icons/)
server/
  index.js         starts the server
  app.js           Express routes: collection, lookup, photos, static client
  collection.js    collection repository (SQLite)
  db.js            database open and schema
  cache.js         HTTP response cache
  lookup.js        merges results from both sources
  metadata/        comics.org client, Inducks search and importer
  scripts/         sync-inducks.js
tests/
  server/          node:test unit and API tests
  e2e/             Playwright specs and the test server harness
  fixtures/        stub comics.org API, Inducks fixture, test images
docs/screenshots/  screenshots used above
```

## Known limitations

- **No authentication.** Anyone who can reach the server can read and change the collection. Only expose it behind a login or on a private network.
- **Series are typed in.** There is no series catalogue. The app remembers the last series you used in the browser.
- **Offline is partial.** The app shell opens offline, but checking, matching, and the collection list need the server.
- **Matches need the sources.** If comics.org or the Inducks index is unavailable, the app says so and still lets you save the issue without details.
- **Inducks freshness depends on the sync.** Until you run `npm run sync:inducks`, Inducks matches are unavailable.
- **Photos are the only record of the cover.** Catalogue details are copied from the match you chose at save time and are not updated later.

- 12 Playwright browser tests pass on Pixel 7 and desktop Chrome. They cover the full journey, the already-owned check, the Inducks path, a failing comics.org, validation, and PWA install/offline. The browser tests run against a stub comics.org and a fixture Inducks index, so they don't depend on the live sites.
- I reviewed the screenshots in `docs/screenshots/`, including the desktop layout.

**Things I fixed along the way**
- Photos stored under a dot-folder path returned 404, because Express refuses dot-prefixed paths by default. That would have hit anyone who set `DATA_DIR` under something like `~/.comics`.
- Cover URLs were being dropped unless they were https, so covers never showed in the match list. Any http(s) URL is now accepted, and other schemes are still rejected.

**Things you should know**
- **There's no login.** Anyone who can reach the server can read and change the collection. Keep it on a private network or behind authentication.
- **Phone install and offline need HTTPS.** Browsers only allow service workers and installation on secure origins. The README covers this.
- **I wiped and rebuilt `data/inducks.sqlite` once by mistake.** A fixture import wrote to the default path. I regenerated the full dataset from the same downloaded files, so the database is complete again.
- **Series is typed in, not chosen from a catalogue.** The app remembers the last series in the browser.
- **Offline is partial.** The shell opens offline, but checking and the collection list need the server.
- **Inducks data goes stale** until you re-run `npm run sync:inducks` and restart the server.

To run it: `npm install`, `npm run sync:inducks`, `npm run build`, `npm start`, then open http://localhost:3000. The README has the full setup, configuration, and testing details.

# Developer entry points. Run `make help` for the list.

GO        ?= go
GOFLAGS   ?= -trimpath
BIN_DIR   := bin
GOLANGCI  ?= golangci-lint
GOVULN    ?= $(shell $(GO) env GOPATH)/bin/govulncheck

.DEFAULT_GOAL := help

.PHONY: help
help: ## Show this help
	@awk 'BEGIN {FS = ":.*##"} /^[a-zA-Z_-]+:.*##/ {printf "  %-12s %s\n", $$1, $$2}' $(MAKEFILE_LIST)

.PHONY: build
build: ## Compile the server and the Inducks sync tool into bin/
	$(GO) build $(GOFLAGS) -o $(BIN_DIR)/server ./cmd/server
	$(GO) build $(GOFLAGS) -o $(BIN_DIR)/sync-inducks ./cmd/sync-inducks

.PHONY: web
web: ## Build the Preact client into dist/
	npm run build

.PHONY: run
run: build web ## Build everything and run the server on PORT (default 3000)
	./$(BIN_DIR)/server

.PHONY: dev
dev: ## Run the API and the Vite dev server together (restart after Go changes)
	npm run dev

.PHONY: sync
sync: build ## Download the Inducks dump and rebuild the local index
	./$(BIN_DIR)/sync-inducks

.PHONY: test
test: ## Run the Go test suite with the race detector
	$(GO) test -race -count=1 ./...

.PHONY: e2e
e2e: ## Run the browser tests (builds everything first)
	npm run test:e2e

.PHONY: vet
vet: ## Run go vet
	$(GO) vet ./...

.PHONY: lint
lint: ## Run golangci-lint (install: brew install golangci-lint)
	$(GOLANGCI) run ./...

.PHONY: vuln
vuln: ## Scan dependencies and code for known vulnerabilities
	$(GO) install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest
	$(GOVULN) ./...

.PHONY: fmt-check
fmt-check: ## Fail if any Go file is not gofmt-formatted
	@test -z "$$(gofmt -l .)" || (echo "gofmt needed:" && gofmt -l . && exit 1)

.PHONY: check
check: fmt-check vet lint test vuln ## Everything CI runs for the Go code

.PHONY: clean
clean: ## Remove build output and test artefacts
	rm -rf $(BIN_DIR) dist tests/.tmp test-results playwright-report

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  go:
    name: Go checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: true
      - name: Verify module checksums
        run: go mod verify
      - name: Check formatting
        run: test -z "$(gofmt -l .)" || (gofmt -l . && exit 1)
      - name: Vet
        run: go vet ./...
      - name: Lint
        uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@v8
        with:
          version: v2.15.0
      - name: Test with race detector
        run: go test -race -count=1 -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
      - name: Known vulnerabilities
        run: |
          go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest
          "$(go env GOPATH)/bin/govulncheck" ./...

  web:
    name: Web client and browser tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: true
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: npm run test:e2e
      - name: Upload Playwright report on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: |
            playwright-report/
            test-results/
          retention-days: 7

info:
  title: Comic Collection API
  version: 0.1.0

  /api/collection:
    get:
      operationId: listCollection
      summary: List every issue in the collection, ordered by series and issue number.
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The collection.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [items, series]
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Comic" }
                  series:
                    type: array
                    items: { type: string }
    post:
      operationId: addComic
      summary: Add an issue with its cover photo.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/NewComic" }
      responses:
        "201":
          description: The issue was saved.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [item]
                properties:
                  item: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Comic" }
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
        "409":
          description: The issue is already in the collection. The existing issue is returned.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [error, item]
                properties:
                  error: { type: string }
                  item: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Comic" }
        "413":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
  /api/collection/check:
    get:
      operationId: checkCollection
      summary: Check whether an issue is already in the collection. Series and number are matched loosely (case, accents and leading zeros are ignored).
      parameters:
        - { $ref: "#/components/parameters/Series" }
        - { $ref: "#/components/parameters/Number" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Ownership result.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [owned]
                properties:
                  owned: { type: boolean }
                  item:
                    oneOf:
                      - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Comic"
                      - type: "null"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
  /api/lookup:
    get:
      operationId: lookupIssue
      summary: Search comics.org and Inducks for candidate matches. Each source reports its own status, so one failing source does not hide the other.
      parameters:
        - { $ref: "#/components/parameters/Series" }
        - { $ref: "#/components/parameters/Number" }
        - name: year
          in: query
          required: false

          schema: { type: string, pattern: "^\\d{4}$" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Candidate matches and per-source status.

              schema:

                required: [series, number, year, candidates, sources]
                properties:
                  series: { type: string }
                  number: { type: string }
                  year: { type: string }
                  candidates:

                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Candidate" }
                  sources:
                    type: object

        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Error"
  /api/comics/{id}:

# haiku-pwa

Stress Test Haiku 5.5

A single-page Progressive Web App for keeping track of a comic book collection by issue number.

- Type a series and an issue number. The app checks your collection and tells you if you already own it.
- If you don't, it looks the issue up on [comics.org](https://www.comics.org) (Grand Comics Database) and [Inducks](https://inducks.org) (Disney comics), lets you pick the matching issue, and asks you to photograph the cover to add it.
- **My collection** lists everything you own, with your photos and links to the catalogue entries.

| Check an issue | Match found on comics.org | Already in your collection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Start screen](docs/screenshots/01-start.png) | ![Match found](docs/screenshots/03-matches-found.png) | ![Already owned](docs/screenshots/06-already-owned.png) |

| My collection | Inducks match | Desktop layout |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![My collection](docs/screenshots/07-my-collection.png) | ![Inducks match](docs/screenshots/09-inducks-match.png) | ![Desktop](docs/screenshots/desktop-03-matches-found.png) |

## Stack

| Part | Technology |
| --- | --- |
| Server and API | Go 1.27, standard library `net/http` routing |
| Database | SQLite through [`modernc.org/sqlite`](https://pkg.go.dev/modernc.org/sqlite), pure Go (no C toolchain needed) |
| Web client | [Preact](https://preactjs.com) + [Vite](https://vite.dev), installable PWA via [vite-plugin-pwa](https://vite-pwa-org.netlify.app) |
| Tests | `go test` with the race detector; [Playwright](https://playwright.dev) for browser tests on phone and desktop profiles |
| Quality gates | `gofmt`, `go vet`, [golangci-lint](https://golangci-lint.run) v2, [govulncheck](https://go.dev/doc/security/vuln/) |
| API contract | [OpenAPI 3.1](api/openapi.yaml) |

## Requirements

- Go 1.27.4 or newer (`go.mod` pins the version; the Go toolchain downloads it automatically if needed)
- Node.js 22.12 or newer, for the web client and the browser tests
- `make` (preinstalled on macOS and Linux)
- For the browser tests only: `npx playwright install chromium`

## Getting started

```sh
npm install
make sync      # one-time: downloads the Inducks database (about 140 MB)
make run       # builds the server and the web client, then serves on http://localhost:3000
```

For development with hot reload in the browser, run `make dev` (or `npm run dev`) and open http://localhost:5173. Vite proxies `/api` to the Go server on port 3000. The Go server does not reload automatically, so restart `make dev` after changing Go code.

To install the app on a phone or use it offline, serve it over HTTPS. Browsers only allow service workers and installation from secure origins.

## How it works

1. **Check.** Enter a series and issue number (and optionally a year). The app asks the server whether that issue is already in the collection. Series names are matched ignoring case and accents, and `05` and `5` are the same issue.
2. **Owned.** If the issue is already there, the app shows your photo and its catalogue details.
3. **Not owned.** The server searches comics.org and Inducks at the same time and lists the candidates with cover art where available. Each source's status is shown, so a failing source does not block the other. Pick the matching issue, or choose *None of these* to save it without details.
4. **Photograph.** Take a photo of the cover with your camera. The browser shrinks it to at most 1280 px before upload.
5. **Save.** The issue, the photo, and the chosen catalogue details are stored locally. **My collection** lists everything, and you can remove items there.

## Data sources

### comics.org (Grand Comics Database)

- Uses the public GCD API (`/api/series/name/{series}/issue/{number}/`, with the optional `/year/{year}/` filter, and `/api/issue/{id}/` for details). No account or API key is needed.
- Variant covers are skipped. Details are fetched for at most eight matches per lookup.
- Requests are rate limited on the client side (two per second, bursts of four), and responses are cached for seven days in the collection database. The service is run by volunteers, so please keep both in place.
- If the service rate-limits the app (HTTP 429), the lookup reports that and the other source still answers.
- GCD data is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Cover images belong to their copyright holders. The app links covers back to the GCD page they came from.

### Inducks

Inducks blocks automated access to its website with a proof-of-work challenge, so the app does not scrape it. Instead, `make sync` (or `go run ./cmd/sync-inducks`):

1. downloads the official daily dump from `https://inducks.org/inducks/isv.tgz`,
2. extracts only the four tables it needs (issues, publications, alternative publication names, country names), and
3. builds a read-only SQLite index in `data/inducks.sqlite`, written to a temporary file and renamed into place only after a complete import.

Re-run the sync to pick up new data. The dump is regenerated daily. Restart the server afterwards so it reopens the new index.

Inducks covers Disney comics such as Topolino and Micky Maus. Its data is available under the [Inducks licence](https://inducks.org/inducks/COPYING). Inducks pictures belong to Disney and are not shown in this app. Matches link to the Inducks issue page instead.

## Configuration

Set these as environment variables.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PORT` | `3000` | HTTP port |
| `DATA_DIR` | `./data` | Where the collection database and photos are stored |
| `WEB_DIR` | `./dist` | The built web client to serve |
| `INDUCKS_DB_PATH` | `$DATA_DIR/inducks.sqlite` | Inducks index built by `make sync` |
| `COMICS_ORG_API_URL` | `https://www.comics.org/api` | comics.org API base URL |
| `LOG_FORMAT` | `text` | `text` or `json` for structured logs |

Invalid values stop the server at startup with a clear message.

## Where your data lives

Everything stays on the machine that runs the server.

- `data/collection.sqlite`: your collection and the comics.org response cache
- `data/photos/`: the photos you took, named by random identifier
- `data/inducks.sqlite`: the Inducks index (rebuilt by the sync)
- `data/inducks-download/`: the downloaded Inducks archive (safe to delete after syncing)

Back up `data/collection.sqlite` and `data/photos/` to keep your collection. Schema changes are applied automatically at startup and tracked with SQLite's `user_version`.

## Testing and quality

```sh
make check     # gofmt, go vet, golangci-lint, race-enabled tests, govulncheck
make e2e       # browser tests: phone and desktop Chromium
```

- **Go tests** cover configuration, normalisation, the collection repository, photo validation, the comics.org client (against an `httptest` server), the Inducks importer and search (run against a small fixture of real Inducks rows), the lookup service, and the HTTP API end to end with a real SQLite file.
- **Browser tests** start a stub comics.org API (`tests/fixtures/stub-comics-org.js`) and the real server with the Inducks fixture. They never touch the live sites or your data. They exercise the whole user journey: entering an issue, matching, photographing, saving, the already-owned check, listing, removing, offline reload, and installability. Screenshots of the phone run are written to `docs/screenshots/`.
- `npm run icons` regenerates the app icons, and `node tests/fixtures/make-fixture-images.mjs` regenerates the test images.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the Go checks and the browser tests on every push and pull request.

## Engineering practices

The backend follows widely used Go practices:

- **Small packages with clear ownership.** `internal/` holds the implementation, so nothing is exposed as a public API by accident. Dependencies point inwards: the HTTP layer depends on the domain packages, never the other way round.
- **Explicit dependencies.** Configuration is read once from the environment and passed down. There is no global state, and sources are injected behind small interfaces.
- **Errors are values.** Errors are wrapped with context using `%w`, matched with `errors.Is` and `errors.As`, and never leak internal details to users. A failing source is reported with a message written for people.
- **Context everywhere.** Request contexts flow into database calls, outbound HTTP requests and the lookup fan-out, so a client that disconnects cancels its work.
- **Safe defaults for network services.** Server read, write, and idle timeouts; a body size limit on uploads; a client timeout and a rate limiter on outbound calls; a bounded response size on outbound reads.
- **Operational basics.** Structured logging with `log/slog` and a request ID on every response; graceful shutdown on SIGINT and SIGTERM; panic recovery that returns a JSON error; a `/api/health` endpoint.
- **Security basics.** Parameterised SQL only; photos validated by sniffing their bytes, not by trusting the declared type; catalogue URLs restricted to http and https; a restrictive Content-Security-Policy and standard security headers; a file server rooted at the web directory so requests cannot escape it.
- **Data integrity.** Migrations are forward-only and versioned. Saving an issue is one transaction that writes the photo atomically and removes it again if the commit fails. The Inducks index is built in a temporary file and only then renamed into place.
- **Tests as specifications.** Table-driven unit tests, real SQLite databases in tests instead of mocks, and browser tests that act as a user would.
- **Automated gates.** `gofmt`, `go vet`, golangci-lint with security and SQL/HTTP-specific linters, the race detector, `govulncheck` for known vulnerabilities, and the API contract in [`api/openapi.yaml`](api/openapi.yaml), linted with Redocly.

## Project layout

```
cmd/
  server/          entry point for the HTTP server
  sync-inducks/    downloads and imports the Inducks dump
internal/
  api/             HTTP routes, handlers, validation, middleware, web-client serving
  catalog/         shared types: queries, candidates, unavailable-source errors
  collection/      the collection repository and key normalisation
  comicsorg/       comics.org API client (rate limited, cached)
  config/         environment configuration
  inducks/         Inducks index search and importer
  lookup/          runs the sources concurrently and merges their results
  photo/           data-URL decoding and image validation
  store/           SQLite opening, migrations and the HTTP cache
    migrations/    versioned schema files
api/openapi.yaml   API contract
client/            Preact app (index.html, src/, public/icons/)
tests/
  e2e/             Playwright specs and the server start script
  fixtures/        stub comics.org API, Inducks fixture, test images
docs/screenshots/  screenshots used above
scripts/           icon generator
```

## Continuous integration

| Job | Steps |
| --- | --- |
| Go checks | module verification, `gofmt`, `go vet`, golangci-lint, race-enabled tests with coverage, govulncheck |
| Web client | `npm ci`, production build, Playwright Chromium, browser tests, report upload on failure |

## Known limitations

- **No authentication.** Anyone who can reach the server can read and change the collection. Only expose it behind a login or on a private network.
- **Series are typed in.** There is no series catalogue. The app remembers the last series you used in the browser.
- **Offline is partial.** The app shell opens offline, but checking, matching, and the collection list need the server.
- **Matches need the sources.** If comics.org is rate limiting or down, or the Inducks index has not been built, the app says so and still lets you save the issue without details.
- **Inducks freshness depends on the sync.** Until you run `make sync`, Inducks matches are unavailable.
- **Catalogue details are a snapshot.** They are copied from the match you chose at save time and are not updated later.
- **Standards.** The practices above follow current, widely used Go and web guidance. I have not verified them against any particular company's internal standard list.

content.text:
Yes, the backend is now Go. The commit is `79de566`, pushed to `origin/main`. The Preact client and the API contract are unchanged, so the UI behaves the same.

**What changed**
- The server and the Inducks sync tool are `cmd/server` and `cmd/sync-inducks`, with the logic under `internal/`. Routing uses the standard `net/http` package, and SQLite runs through `modernc.org/sqlite`, which is pure Go.
- The Node server is gone. Node remains only for the Vite build, the Playwright tests, and the stub comics.org that the browser tests use.
- Day-to-day commands: `make run`, `make sync`, and `make check`. `make check` runs gofmt, `go vet`, golangci-lint, race-enabled tests, and govulncheck.

**On "Forbes 500 standards"**
I couldn't find or verify a list like that, so I haven't claimed to meet one. I applied widely used Go and web practices and listed them in the README's Engineering practices section. The API is documented as OpenAPI 3.1 in `api/openapi.yaml`. It validates under Redocly with four warnings I left on purpose: the `localhost` server URL and missing 4xx responses on two GET endpoints.

**Verified**
- All Go packages pass with the race detector. golangci-lint reports 0 issues, and govulncheck finds no known vulnerabilities.
- All 12 browser tests pass against the Go binary.
- `make sync` ran the real download end to end: 134 MiB fetched, then 264,103 issues imported.

**Problems I found and fixed**
- The Go store didn't create its data directory, so a fresh install would have failed at startup. It now does, with a regression test.
- The import logs counted attempted rows rather than stored rows. They now count what was actually written.
- comics.org returned HTTP 429 during my testing. I added a client-side limiter (one request per second, bursts of three) and a plain-language message for users.

I can't verify live comics.org results right now, because the service is still rate limiting this address. Live Inducks lookups work.

**Needs your decision: a stray commit**
Commit `5afb19a` ("add session transcript") was already on your local `main`, and my `git push` sent it to GitHub. It adds a 3.3 MB session export, `session-dc1ad668-….json`, to the repo root. I didn't create it. It contains about 117 lines that match secret-like words, and I haven't read them in full.

Options:
1. Delete the file in a new commit and add it to `.gitignore`. This is non-destructive, but the contents remain in history.
2. Rewrite history to remove the commit and force-push. This is destructive, so I won't do it without your go-ahead.

If the repository is public or the transcript holds credentials, I'd recommend option 2. Which would you like?
